(NASDAQ: SPCX ) is reportedly planning to raise $40 billion in bank loans and investment-grade debt, led by Apollo Global Management (NYSE: APO ) , to buy Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA ) chips. Seeks $10 Billion in Loans, $30 Billion in Debt The Elon Musk -led company is looking to raise about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt for the chip order, Reuters News reported, citing the Financial Times. Apollo is expected to lead the deal and help place the debt with a broad range of investors, with Pimco among a small group of lenders in talks to provide financing, the newspaper reported citing people familiar with the matter. The transaction is expected to close in 2027. SpaceX, Apollo, Nvidia, and Pimco did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment. Inc. , on financing platforms meant to mobilize more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure. Big Tech is leaning more on debt to fund the AI buildout. Amazon.com Inc. , Microsoft Corp. , Alphabet Inc. , Meta Platforms Inc., and Oracle Corp. issued about $200 billion of investment-grade debt in the first half of 2026, nearly double their issuance in all of 2025, according to iShares. AI spending across the hyperscaler ecosystem could rise from roughly $700 billion this year to $1 trillion in 2027, according to JPMorgan Chase. He said last month that the Colossus 2 data center could more than double its Nvidia chips by December. title: Most Undervalued Chip Stocks In October 2026: Four Are Cheaper Than The S&P 500
description: Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ: MU ) tops the list of the most undervalued chip stocks in October, gaining more than 460% in 12 months. The memory chip maker trades at 6 times forward earnings. That’s according to TradingView’s latest screener data on the 28 U.S.-listed members of the PHLX Semiconductor Sector index. The forward price-to-earnings ratio (forward P/E) divides the share price by the profit analysts expect over the next year. A lower number means investors pay less for each dollar of expected profit. By comparison, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE: SPY ) trades at 20.3 times next-12-month earnings. Four chip stocks currently trade at cheaper valuations than the broader market: Micron, NXP Semiconductors N.V. (NASDAQ: NXPI ) , Qualcomm Inc. (NASDAQ: QCOM ) and Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA ) . Microchip Technology Inc. (NASDAQ: MCHP ) sits just above it. So why is the market paying less than the index for the industry driving U.S. earnings growth? Company Forward P/E Market cap 1-year change Micron Technology 6.01 $1.18 trillion +460.60% NXP Semiconductors 14.62 $61.62 billion +4.58% Qualcomm 19.58 $193.31 billion +6.11% Nvidia 19.93 $5.77 trillion +27.70% S&P 500 (SPY) 20.30 — — Microchip Technology 20.61 $44.12 billion +23.13% Source: TradingView, Koyfin (SPY next-12-month P/E) Undervalued Chip Stocks Start With Micron’s Memory Boom Micron’s largest business is DRAM (dynamic random-access memory), the short-term memory that servers, PCs and phones use to run programs. Demand for that memory has outrun supply because of artificial intelligence. As a result, prices have surged. Micron sold 211% more DRAM in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 than a year earlier, according to its latest quarterly filing. Average selling prices rose about 140%, while volumes grew about 30%. Consequently, profitability exploded. Gross margin, the share of revenue left after the cost of making the product, reached 85% in the fiscal third quarter. A year earlier, it was 38%. Why The Market Doesn’t Trust Micron’s Earnings Yet Memory has always been a cyclical business. High prices push manufacturers to build new factories. New factories create too much supply. Then prices fall, and margins shrink. As a result, investors tend to put low multiples on memory stocks when profits peak. A low forward P/E does not mean the market missed the boom. Instead, it signals doubt that these earnings can last. The key question now is whether AI has changed the rules for Micron. If memory demand now grows every year, instead of rising and falling with the cycle, a multiple of 6 would be too low. NXP And Qualcomm Are Cheap For Different Reasons NXP trades at 14.6 times forward earnings, even as its business accelerates. The Dutch chipmaker reported second-quarter revenue of $3.5 billion, up 19% from a year earlier. “AI is moving from the cloud into the physical world — into vehicles, factories, and robots,” Chief Executive Rafael Sotomayor said in the results release. NXP expects third-quarter revenue of $3.75 billion. However, the stock has gained only 4.58% over the past year. Meanwhile, Qualcomm’s fiscal third-quarter revenue fell 4% to $9.9 billion. Handset chip revenue dropped 20% to $5.1 billion, as Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL ) shifts to its own modems. Its automotive revenue, however, jumped 61% to a record $1.6 billion. The company targets $40 billion in non-handset revenue by fiscal 2029. Read Also: US Economy Kept Growing For 78 Months: These 10 Stocks Top The Leaderboard Nvidia Is Now Cheaper Than The S&P 500 Nvidia, the world’s largest company by market value, trades at 19.9 times forward earnings — below the multiple of the overall index. Yet its growth is nothing like the index’s. Nvidia’s second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue more than doubled to $96.2 billion. Data center revenue rose 117% to $89.0 billion. “AI has reached its inflection point,” founder and CEO Jensen Huang said in the earnings release. “Now, compute is revenue.” The stock has risen 27.70% over the past year, while revenue grew 106%. In other words, profits have grown faster than the share price, and the multiple has compressed. Cheap For A Reason, Or Cheap By Mistake? A forward P/E is only as good as the estimates behind it. If memory prices fall or AI spending slows, analysts would cut their forecasts, and today’s low multiples would no longer look so low. On the other hand, if AI demand proves more durable than past chip cycles, the market may be underpricing the companies at the center of the buildout. For now, the S&P 500 costs more than the chipmakers supplying its biggest growth story. (NASDAQ: SPCX ) CEO Elon Musk and other leading tech executives will reportedly receive the nation’s highest honors for scientific and technological achievement from President Donald Trump on Thursday. White House Summit to Honor Tech Leaders Trump will award the National Medal of Science to Musk, Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) co-founder Sergey Brin , Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang , and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ: AMD ) CEO Lisa Su , Fox News Digital reported on Wednesday. Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE: DELL ) CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ: MSFT ) CEO Satya Nadella will receive the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. The awards will be presented at the White House’s Science: A New Golden Age Summit. It will be the first time Trump has presented either medal in either of his administrations. “The Trump administration is grateful for the contributions of these incredible leaders in science and technology. These recipients are helping ensure America keeps leading the world in innovation,” White House spokesperson Liz Huston told Fox News. The White House did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment. According to a July report by The New York Times, Musk plans to spend $100 million to $120 million backing at least eight GOP candidates in the midterms. Huang donated to Trump’s White House ballroom . Dell has pledged $6.25 billion to fund accounts for 25 million children under Trump’s accounts program. AMD has also contributed to the effort . AI Leaders Signed on to Trump’s Safety Pledge Last month, Trump hosted AI and tech leaders at the White House for the Accord on Super Intelligence , a voluntary safety pact calling for independent audits, stronger internal controls, and board-level oversight of advanced AI systems. title: Jim Cramer Says SPCX Could Come to Fruition Long Before Tesla After Goldman Sachs Raises Price Target: 'Real Company With Real Numbers'
description: TV Host Jim Cramer has praised Elon Musk ‘s commercial spaceflight company Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ: SPCX ) , saying that the enterprise could benefit investors even before Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ: TSLA ) did. SpaceX Is a ‘Real Company’ With a ‘Real Business’ On Wednesday, Cramer hailed SpaceX on the “Mad Money” show on CNBC, saying that Musk had made some “very smart moves” by renting out excess AI compute with NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ: NVDA ) chips that Cramer said Musk bought at “extortionate prices,” while also pointing to the compute deals with Anthropic and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) (NASDAQ: GOOG ) . Read Also: Jeff Bezos Just Put Blue Origin's IPO on the Radar After $10 Billion Funding Round: 'It Probably Makes Sense' “I’ve been adamant this [SpaceX] is a real company with real numbers and a real business, many businesses even,” Cramer said, adding that he had defended the company against criticism that it was overvalued . Goldman Sachs Price Target Cramer then pointed to Goldman Sachs Group Inc. (NYSE: GS ) raising its price target for SpaceX to $230, which “ratified” the previous $220 price target. “When you’re dealing with real speculative games, you almost never see price target bumps until after the hot money’s over on the price target. By then, it’s too late anyway,” Cramer said. However, Cramer then said that he understood the investment bank’s price target bump, adding that SpaceX was making “so much money renting out compute” that it was planning to borrow $40 billion to buy more NVIDIA chips . “SpaceX could end up being NVIDIA’s largest client at this pace. That’s fantastic news for both sides,” he said. The TV Host then said that it was “becoming more and more likely that SpaceX could come to fruition a lot earlier than Tesla ever did.” Morgan Stanley Bullish on SpaceX Notably, Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS ) analyst Adam Jonas said that the company presented a “unique” investment opportunity with its wide array of “interlinked” businesses and that it was “unusually cheap” when investors factored in the opportunities in chipmaking and power. Jonas reiterated an “overweight” rating for SpaceX and issued a price target of $300 for SpaceX shares, illustrating bullish sentiment on the stock. SpaceX Is a ‘Real Company’ With a ‘Real Business’ On Wednesday, Cramer hailed SpaceX on the “Mad Money” show on CNBC, saying that Musk had made some “very smart moves” by renting out excess AI compute with NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ: NVDA ) chips that Cramer said Musk bought at “extortionate prices,” while also pointing to the compute deals with Anthropic and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) (NASDAQ: GOOG ) . Goldman Sachs Price Target Cramer then pointed to Goldman Sachs Group Inc. (NYSE: GS ) raising its price target for SpaceX to $230, which “ratified” the previous $220 price target. “When you’re dealing with real speculative games, you almost never see price target bumps until after the hot money’s over on the price target. By then, it’s too late anyway,” Cramer said. However, Cramer then said that he understood the investment bank’s price target bump, adding that SpaceX was making “so much money renting out compute” that it was planning to borrow $40 billion to buy more NVIDIA chips . “SpaceX could end up being NVIDIA’s largest client at this pace. That’s fantastic news for both sides,” he said. The TV Host then said that it was “becoming more and more likely that SpaceX could come to fruition a lot earlier than Tesla ever did.” Morgan Stanley Bullish on SpaceX Notably, Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS ) analyst Adam Jonas said that the company presented a “unique” investment opportunity with its wide array of “interlinked” businesses and that it was “unusually cheap” when investors factored in the opportunities in chipmaking and power. Jonas reiterated an “overweight” rating for SpaceX and issued a price target of $300 for SpaceX shares, illustrating bullish sentiment on the stock. title: What Is Going on With Palantir Tech Stock on Thursday?
description: Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ: PLTR ) is drawing fresh investor attention as bullish AI spending expectations, accelerating U.S. commercial demand and continued government work reinforce its position across enterprise and public-sector technology. The stock gained more than 2% in Thursday premarket trading even as S&P 500 futures fell about 0.4%. UK Contract Extension Adds Public-Sector Revenue Palantir expanded the value of its U.K. government work after the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government extended its Homes for Ukraine contract by another year and 5 million Pounds (roughly $6.60 million). The extension brought total payments to 15 million pounds (roughly $19.80 million), the Financial Times reported on Thursday. The deal highlighted Palantir’s role in supporting a major public program even as the U.K. government developed an in-house alternative and reviewed its broader reliance on the company. Palantir said it built the refugee-support system in nine days and later helped the government transition to its own platform. Dan Ives Sees Palantir Among 2027 Tech Leaders Yorkville Ives & Co. Senior Managing Director Dan Ives included Palantir among his top technology picks for 2027, arguing that investors are underestimating the scale of a coming $4 trillion spending wave . Ives ranked Palantir third among his five preferred technology names, alongside NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA ) , Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ: MSFT ) , Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL ) and CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: CRWD ) . He views the expected spending cycle as a multiyear shift in enterprise technology investment that could support established leaders across data analytics, software, semiconductors and cybersecurity. Analysts Remain Bullish Palantir carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $202.46. Rosenblatt maintained a Buy rating and $225 forecast on Sept. 23. UBS raised its Buy-rated forecast to $250 on Sept. 15, while DA Davidson also lifted its Buy-rated forecast to $250 on Sept. 11. Technical Read Palantir Technologies Inc. ‘s stock has a strong bullish setup, trading well above its 20-, 50-, 100-, and 200-day moving averages while both the short- and long-term averages point higher. This shows broad trend strength, though the wide gap from the longer-term averages also leaves room for a pullback if momentum cools. RSI is 78.20, firmly in overbought territory after entering that zone on September 27. Momentum is powerful, but traders should be ready for consolidation or a sharp retracement rather than assume the current pace can continue uninterrupted. MACD is above its signal line, indicating bullish momentum. That supports the uptrend, but traders should watch for a bearish cross if buying pressure fades, especially with RSI already stretched. Palantir Technologies’s stock has support near 164.50 and resistance around 207.50. Holding above support would keep the bullish trend intact, while a decisive break above resistance could signal a fresh continuation move; failure at resistance could instead trigger a pullback toward lower moving averages. The golden cross in September, when the 50-day SMA moved above the 200-day SMA, reinforced the longer-term bullish trend. With the 20-day SMA also above the 50-day SMA, Palantir Technologies Inc.’s stock has a favorable moving-average structure that traders will want to protect. Palantir Technologies Inc.’s stock is up 8.13% over the past 12 months, showing a positive longer-term trend even though the gain is smaller than the recent surge implied by its position near the 52-week high. The stock is currently at 91.7% of that range, so continued upside would require a clean breakout rather than simply recovering from a deeply depressed level. The recent swing low on July 27 and the 52-week low on June 24 marked the base from which this advance developed, while the October 1 swing high shows that buyers have pushed price close to its upper boundary. Traders should focus on whether momentum can produce a sustained breakout or whether overbought conditions lead to a reset before the next leg higher. PLTR Price Action: Palantir Technologies shares were up 2.59% at $199.15 during premarket trading on Thursday. The stock is approaching its 52-week high of $207.52, according to Benzinga Pro data . title: Jeff Bezos Hints at Blue Origin IPO After $10 Billion Funding Round — Amazon Founder Says It ‘Makes Sense’ for SpaceX Rival to Go 'Public' (UPDATED)
description: Editor’s Note: The story has been updated with additional details and a new headline. Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN ) founder Jeff Bezos said that Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX ) rival Blue Origin could eventually go public after the space company secured $10 billion in a funding round that reportedly valued it at $140 billion . Bezos Signals Blue Origin IPO On Wednesday, speaking on Fox News Channel’s "Special Report with Bret Baier," Bezos said an initial public offering could happen "several years from now," suggesting a stock market debut is part of Blue Origin’s longer-term plans. "I think, someday, Blue Origin will have an IPO; exactly when that will be, I don’t know," Bezos said, adding that "it probably makes sense for Blue Origin to be a public company at some point." The Amazon founder said he has invested approximately $28 billion in the space company since launching it in 2000. Read Also: Amazon AI Boom: Analysts See AWS, AI Agents Driving Bigger Growth $10 Billion Raise Values Blue Origin At $140 Billion The company’s latest funding round marks its first major capital raise from outside investors. Bezos said he didn’t want outside investors until now, but he now sees the "financial future of Blue with some clarity now." Blue Origin has secured multibillion-dollar contracts from NASA and the U.S. Space Force, including work tied to NASA’s Artemis lunar program. It still competes with Elon Musk’s Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ: SPCX ) in the commercial launch market. New Glenn Targets December Return Blue Origin is also preparing to resume New Glenn launches after a May explosion during a static-fire test delayed its launch plans. Bezos said the company expects to fly the rocket again in December. "December of this year, we’re going to fly that vehicle again," Bezos said. title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus Scraps Australia’s Second-Largest IPO Plan After Poor Demand and Volatile Market: 'Not in the Best Interests…'
description: Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA ) -backed Firmus has reportedly shelved its AUD $7.1 billion ($4.95 billion) initial public offering in Australia after poor demand and volatile market conditions, and will raise money privately instead. Turns to Private Markets “Firmus will now pursue capital from the private markets and consider alternative public and private market options,” the company said, according to Reuters. The terms did not accurately reflect the strength of its business and its long-term growth outlook, the data center operator added. “The board therefore concluded that proceeding with the offer was not in the best interests of the company and its shareholders,” it said. The company cited market volatility and conditions as reasons to shelve the offering. The offering would have been the second-largest new share sale in Australia’s history, but it failed to draw strong demand. Firmus did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment . Read Also: Elon Musk Hypes ‘Very Big Deal,’ but Cathie Wood Hits Sell on SpaceX Along With Meta, AMD and Google — Ark Loads Up on This Defense Stock IPO Would Have Valued Firmus At $30.6 Billion Firmus had planned to sell shares at AUD $11 ($7.67) each, valuing it at $30.6 billion, nearly triple the $10.5 billion valuation from a funding round in August. In that round, the company raised $2 billion from investors including Nvidia, Coatue , Blackstone Inc. (NYSE: BX ) and Jane Street . Last month, Firmus announced agreements with Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ: META on Sept. 29 for GPU compute capacity at its AI factories in Southeast Asia. A Cooling IPO Market Seven sizable U.S. IPOs were postponed or pulled in the third quarter, up from four in the second, according to Vested. Smart-ring maker Oura postponed a $2.2 billion listing on Sept. 29, citing market uncertainty. Higher bond yields and interest rates have weighed on new listings, with the 10-year Treasury yield hitting its highest level since 2002 this week, while the 30-year yield climbed to a 24-year high. description: Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ: META ) has immediately barred TikTok parent ByteDance from advertising on Facebook and Instagram in seven countries. Meta Blocks ByteDance Ads In 7 Countries The ban covers the U.S., Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand and Vietnam, a Meta spokesperson told Benzinga on Thursday. It also applies to third-party advertisers running campaigns that direct users to TikTok and other ByteDance-owned properties in those markets. The new joint venture is 80.1% owned by global investors, including Oracle Corp. (NYSE: ORCL ) , while ByteDance retains a 19.9% stake. Despite the ownership arrangement, TikTok remains a major competitor to Meta. Bloomberg News first reported the advertising ban on Thursday. title: Is OpenAI’s ‘ChatGPT For Teens’ Unsafe? New Study Sparks Concern | Details
description: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens in August with promises of stronger protections, parental notifications for high-risk conversations, and safeguards against emotional dependence. Common Sense Media’s Youth AI Safety Institute tested more than 4,000 prompts and found the product’s safety features failed to reliably detect mental health crises, notify parents, or prevent students from bypassing learning safeguards. In some areas, performance was worse after the teen version launched. Parental alerts were almost non-existent: zero notifications arrived within an hour despite explicit crisis disclosures. Crisis hotline referrals dropped, and three severe-harm categories failed the institute’s 95% detection benchmark. Students could also easily bypass study-mode restrictions.

description: Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN ) is reportedly weighing a roughly $7 billion purchase of Decart , an artificial intelligence startup whose software helps developers switch between chips. Deal Could Close Soon A deal could come together soon, the Wall Street Journal reported , citing people familiar with the matter, although the talks could collapse or another bidder could step in. Amazon Web Services gave Decart early access to its custom Trainium3 chip in 2025, and the startup’s chip-switching capability is becoming more important as companies race to secure computing power. Trainium is a family of custom AI chips developed by AWS to train and run machine learning and generative AI models. The chip competes with processors from Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA ) . Amazon declined to comment on the report, noting that it does not comment on speculation. Decart did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request. Amazon is effectively buying software expertise to improve Trainium utilization and make its custom silicon more attractive as AI workloads expand… pic.twitter.com/MepmWCixQA — Shay Boloor (@StockSavvyShay) October 11, 2026 Anthropic Reportedly Walked Away From Decart Decart was also a reported target for Anthropic , which Bloomberg reported in September had abandoned talks to buy the startup for about $6 billion. The company, founded in 2023 by Dean Leitersdorf , Moshe Shalev , and Orian Leitersdorf , builds real-time generative video and interactive world models, including Oasis and Lucy. It raised $300 million in a Series B round in May, led by Radical Ventures , with Nvidia among the investors, pushing its valuation to nearly $4 billion. Existing investors Sequoia Capital, Benchmark, and Zeev Ventures were also involved. Price Action: On Friday, Amazon closed 3.29% higher at $262.43 and gained 0.038% to $262.53 in extended trading. The managing partners estimate that 100 million subscribers paying $20 per month could generate about $24 billion annually, roughly 6% of Apple’s revenue. title: SK Hynix Stock Plunges 11% in Seoul, Slips After Hours in New York as Hot CPI, Fed Hike Bets and AI Funding Worries Weigh
description: SK Hynix Inc. (NASDAQ: SKHY ) shares tumbled more than 11% in Seoul on Thursday, deepening a global chip selloff tied to hotter U.S. inflation, Federal Reserve rate-hike bets and doubts over funding the artificial intelligence buildout. SK Hynix Leads Asia’s Chip Rout The chipmaker fell 11.42% at the time of writing to KRW 1,257,000 ($929.92), while Samsung Electronics fell 8.84% to KRW 211,500 ($156.47). South Korea’s KOSPI fell 7.81% to 5,539.34. In Japan, the Nikkei fell 225 fell 4.12% to 64,951.15, with SoftBank Group Corp falling 9.34%. On Wall Street Wednesday, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 1.88% to 26,692.87, and the S&P 500 slid 1.11% to 7,718.94, with technology shares leading the losses. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ: SOXX ) , which has gained more than 70% this year, has lost money in each of the past seven sessions . Read Also: CoreWeave, Rocket Lab, Dell, Greenland Energy Company and Bending Spoons: Why These 5 Stocks Are on Investors' Radars Today Hot CPI Revives Rate-Hike Fears U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% year over year in September, up from 3.4% in August, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The Federal Reserve raised rates to a range of 3.75% to 4% on Sept. 16, and one more hike is expected this year. AI Financing Worries Build Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO ) (NASDAQ: AVGO ) CEO Hock Tan said Monday at a conference in Singapore that access to capital could become a bigger obstacle for AI than chip or power shortages, while Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC ) CEO Lip-Bu Tan flagged rising financing costs and uncertainty over investment returns. Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE: GS ) CEO David Solomon said the 10-year Treasury yield has risen about 75 basis points since early July and warned that not every data center project will win financing on favorable terms. Tech analyst Dan Ives said that the pullback is a buying opportunity and that the AI boom is still in its early stages, according to CNBC. Price Action: SK Hynix’s Nasdaq-listed ADRs closed 6.06% lower on Wednesday at $147.55 and fell 3.96% to $141.71 in extended trading. title: Vadzo Imaging Validates Low Noise Imaging on Bolt-521CRS: Onsemi AR0521 5MP Color MIPI CSI-2 Camera with RK3588 Rockchip Processor
description: The Bolt-521CRS is a 5MP Color MIPI CSI-2 Camera built on the Onsemi AR0521 sensor, and Vadzo has validated its low-noise imaging on the RK3588 Rockchip processor. Noise decides how useful an embedded image is. It hides detail in dim scenes, confuses detection models, and inflates the bitrate of recorded video. Where that noise gets controlled matters as much as how much of it there is, because a raw sensor module leaves denoising, color processing, and tuning to the host, and the result depends on how well the host was tuned. The Bolt-521CRS takes a different route. Large 2.2-micron pixels gather more light, and an on-board image signal processor applies denoising, color correction, and auto exposure inside the module, so the host receives a finished YUV image. As a Low Noise Embedded Camera, it delivers Full HD at up to 60 frames per second and 5MP at up to 30 frames per second. Designed for smart surveillance, warehouse robotics, and medical and life science devices, this RK3588 Compatible MIPI Camera gives embedded teams a clean, consistent image on Rockchip, Raspberry Pi, and NVIDIA platforms.

title: Surf Air Mobility Expands Palantir-Powered AI Push With Fifth Aviation Software Deal
description: Surf Air Mobility Inc. (NYSE: SRFM ) announced Thursday that it signed a software agreement with Flying Zebra , marking its fifth commercial contract for OperatorOS, an artificial intelligence-powered aviation platform developed with Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ: PLTR ) . The agreement brings Surf Air Mobility closer to its goal of having five operators actively using the platform by the end of 2026 . Surf Air Mobility Expands AI Aviation Software Business Under the agreement, Surf Air Mobility will receive a percentage of revenue from every Flying Zebra trip managed through OperatorOS. The company did not disclose the financial terms. Flying Zebra operates four aircraft. The software will help the operator manage aircraft and crew schedules, improve operational visibility and reduce manual work. OperatorOS, part of Surf Air Mobility’s SurfOS platform, uses AI to streamline flight management, reporting and distribution for commercial charter operators. SurfOS President Barrett Brown said the company has secured five OperatorOS agreements and is now focused on bringing those customers onto the platform before year-end. The software has supported Surf Air Mobility’s Southern Airways and Mokulele Airlines operations since 2025. It also recently received Federal Aviation Administration approval for electronic signatures and recordkeeping. SurfOS Helps Cut Operating Costs The latest agreement follows an Oct. 7 operational update, in which Surf Air Mobility highlighted efficiency gains from its software platform . During the first nine months of 2026, the company reported a 6% reduction in direct operating costs per block hour, alongside a 9% decline in fuel consumption and pilot costs per block hour. Labor productivity per block hour improved 15%, while Mokulele Airlines’ second-quarter revenue increased approximately 7% year over year. The company also secured a four-year, $19.4 million federal subsidy contract to continue serving Lanaʻi, Hawaii, through August 2030. Meanwhile, Surf Air Mobility is expanding its electric aviation plans following 64 demonstration flights conducted with BETA Technologies across four Hawaiian islands. The company aims to improve airline profitability while expanding SurfOS adoption among third-party operators, creating additional software-related revenue opportunities.
